   121→        return;

   123→
   124→    spacecraftBlacklistJson.clear();
   125→
   126→    spacecraftBlacklistJson["TEST"] = true;
   127→    spacecraftBlacklistJson["DSN"] = true;
   128→    spacecraftBlacklistJson["RFC(VLBI)"] = true;
   129→    spacecraftBlacklistJson["GO19"] = true;
   130→
   131→    if (serializeJson(spacecraftBlacklistJson, file) == 0) {
   132→        Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "Failed to write to blacklist.json" + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   133→        return;
   134→    }
   135→
   136→    file.close();

   140→/* Check Name */
   141→const char* SpacecraftData::callsignToName(const char* key) {
   142→    bool showSerial = FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial;
   143→
   144→    if (showSerial) {
   145→        char buffer[256];
   146→        snprintf(
   147→            buffer,
   148→            sizeof(buffer),
   149→            "%s>>> Checking names lookup for %s...%s\n",
   150→            DevUtils::termColor("yellow"),
   151→            key,
   152→            DevUtils::termColor("reset")
   153→        );
   154→        Serial.print(buffer);
   155→    }
   156→
   157→    if (spacecraftNamesJson.containsKey(key)) {
   158→        if (showSerial)
   159→            Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("green") + "Found spacecraft name for " + String(key) + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   160→        const char* spacecraftName = spacecraftNamesJson[key];
   161→        return spacecraftName;
   162→    }
   163→
   164→    if (showSerial) {
   165→        Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "Spacecraft name not found for " + String(key) + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   166→    }
   167→
   168→    // Spacecraft name not found, return the callsign
   169→    return key;
   170→}
   171→
   172→/* Check Blacklist */
   173→bool SpacecraftData::checkBlacklist(const char* key) {
   174→    bool showSerial = FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial;
   175→    bool isBlacklisted = spacecraftBlacklistJson[key] != nullptr; // If the key is not null, it is blacklisted
   176→
   177→    if (showSerial) {
   178→        char buffer[128];
   179→        if (isBlacklisted) {
   180→            snprintf(
   181→                buffer,
   182→                sizeof(buffer),
   183→                "%s%s is blacklisted, skipping...%s\n", 
   184→                DevUtils::termColor("purple"), 
   185→                key, 
   186→                DevUtils::termColor("reset")
   187→            );
   188→            Serial.print(buffer);
   189→        }
   190→    }
   191→
   192→    return isBlacklisted;
   193→}

    58→
    59→void FileUtils::listDir(const char* dirname, uint8_t levels) {
    60→	Serial.printf("Listing directory: %s\r\n", dirname);
    61→
    62→	File root = LittleFS.open(dirname);
    63→	if (!root) {
    64→		Serial.println("- failed to open directory");
    65→		return;
    66→	}
    67→	if (!root.isDirectory()) {
    68→		Serial.println(" - not a directory");
    69→		return;
    70→	}
    71→
    72→	File file = root.openNextFile();
    73→	while (file) {
    74→		if (file.isDirectory()) {
    75→			Serial.print("  DIR : ");
    76→
    77→			Serial.print(file.name());
    78→			time_t t = file.getLastWrite();
    79→			struct tm* tmstruct = localtime(&t);
    80→			Serial.printf("  LAST WRITE: %d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d\n", (tmstruct->tm_year) + 1900, (tmstruct->tm_mon) + 1, tmstruct->tm_mday, tmstruct->tm_hour, tmstruct->tm_min, tmstruct->tm_sec);
    81→
    82→			if (levels) {
    83→				listDir(file.name(), levels - 1);
    84→			}
    85→		} else {
    86→			Serial.print("  FILE: ");
    87→			Serial.print(file.name());
    88→			Serial.print("  SIZE: ");
    89→
    90→			Serial.print(file.size());
    91→			time_t t = file.getLastWrite();
    92→			struct tm* tmstruct = localtime(&t);
    93→			Serial.printf("  LAST WRITE: %d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d\n", (tmstruct->tm_year) + 1900, (tmstruct->tm_mon) + 1, tmstruct->tm_mday, tmstruct->tm_hour, tmstruct->tm_min, tmstruct->tm_sec);
    94→		}
    95→		file = root.openNextFile();
    96→	}
    97→}
    98→
    99→void FileUtils::listFilesystem(const char* dirname, int8_t loop = 0) {
   100→	// Serial.printf("Listing directory: %s\r\n", dirname);
   101→
   102→	File root = LittleFS.open(dirname);
   103→	if (!root) {
   104→		Serial.println("- failed to open directory");
   105→		return;
   106→	}
   107→	if (!root.isDirectory()) {
   108→		Serial.println(" - not a directory");
   109→		return;
   110→	}
   111→
   112→	File file = root.openNextFile();
   113→	while (file) {
   114→		for (int8_t i = 0; i < loop; i++) {
   115→			Serial.print("    ");
   116→		}
   117→
   118→		Serial.print("└──");
   119→
   120→		if (file.isDirectory()) {
   121→			Serial.print("/");
   122→			Serial.print(file.name());
   123→			time_t t = file.getLastWrite();
   124→			struct tm* tmstruct = localtime(&t);
   125→			Serial.printf(
   126→				"  LAST WRITE: %d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d\n",
   127→				(tmstruct->tm_year) + 1900, (tmstruct->tm_mon) + 1,
   128→				tmstruct->tm_mday, tmstruct->tm_hour,
   129→				tmstruct->tm_min, tmstruct->tm_sec
   130→			);
   131→
   132→			// Create a new path with leading '/'
   133→			String newPath = String(dirname) + "/" + file.name();
   134→			listFilesystem(newPath.c_str(), loop + 1);
   135→		} else {
   136→			Serial.print(" ");
   137→			Serial.print(file.name());
   138→			Serial.print("  SIZE: ");
   139→			Serial.print(file.size());
   140→			time_t t = file.getLastWrite();
   141→			struct tm* tmstruct = localtime(&t);
   142→			Serial.printf(
   143→				"  LAST WRITE: %d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d\n",
   144→				(tmstruct->tm_year) + 1900, (tmstruct->tm_mon) + 1,
   145→				tmstruct->tm_mday, tmstruct->tm_hour,
   146→				tmstruct->tm_min, tmstruct->tm_sec
   147→			);
   148→		}
   149→		file = root.openNextFile();
   150→	}
   151→}

   153→void FileUtils::createDir(const char* path) {
   154→	// prinmt free heap
   155→	Serial.print("Free heap: " + String(ESP.getFreeHeap()) + "\n");
   156→	Serial.printf("Creating Dir: %s\n", path);
   157→	try {
   158→		if (LittleFS.mkdir(path)) {
   159→			Serial.println("Dir created");
   160→		} else {
   161→			Serial.println("mkdir failed");
   162→		}
   163→	} catch (const std::exception& e) {
   164→		Serial.println(e.what());
   165→	}
   166→}
   167→
   168→void FileUtils::removeDir(const char* path) {
   169→	Serial.printf("Removing Dir: %s\n", path);
   170→	if (LittleFS.rmdir(path)) {
   171→		Serial.println("Dir removed");
   172→	} else {
   173→		Serial.println("rmdir failed");
   174→	}
   175→}
   176→
   177→void FileUtils::readFile(const char* path) {
   178→	Serial.printf("Reading file: %s\r\n", path);
   179→
   180→	File file = LittleFS.open(path);
   181→	if (!file || file.isDirectory()) {
   182→		Serial.println("- failed to open file for reading");
   183→		return;
   184→	}
   185→
   186→	Serial.println("- read from file:");
   187→	while (file.available()) {
   188→		Serial.write(file.read());
   189→	}
   190→	file.close();
   191→}
   192→
   193→void FileUtils::writeFile(const char* path, const char* message) {
   194→	Serial.printf("Writing file: %s\r\n", path);
   195→
   196→	File file = LittleFS.open(path, FILE_WRITE);
   197→	if (!file) {
   198→		Serial.println("- failed to open file for writing");
   199→		return;
   200→	}
   201→	if (file.print(message)) {
   202→		Serial.println("- file written");
   203→	} else {
   204→		Serial.println("- write failed");
   205→	}
   206→	file.close();
   207→}
   208→
   209→void FileUtils::appendFile(const char* path, const char* message) {

   217→	if (file.print(message)) {
   218→		Serial.println("- message appended");

   220→		Serial.println("- append failed");
   221→	}
   222→	file.close();
   223→}

     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→Replace hardcoded spacecraft data with remotely-hosted JSON files fetched from GitHub and cached on LittleFS. Add a portal setting to toggle between a "full" callsign list and a NASA-approved "restricted" list.
     6→
     7→## Background
     8→
     9→### Current Behavior
    10→
    11→`SpacecraftData.cpp` hardcodes all spacecraft data in three `createAndWrite*()` functions:
    12→
    13→1. **`createAndWriteNamesFile()`** — 81 callsign→name mappings, written to `/spacecraft_data/names.json`
    14→2. **`createAndWriteBlacklistFile()`** — 3-4 always-filtered callsigns, written to `/spacecraft_data/blacklist.json`
    15→3. **`createAndWritePlaceholderRatesFile()`** — 26 spacecraft with fallback rate arrays, written to `/spacecraft_data/placeholder_rates.json`
    16→
    17→On every boot, these functions **overwrite** the LittleFS files with hardcoded data, then the `load*()` functions read them back into `DynamicJsonDocument` objects. This means updating any spacecraft requires a firmware update.
    18→
    19→### Problems
    20→
    21→- Adding/removing spacecraft requires a new firmware build and OTA
    22→- The NASA client approved a limited subset of craft, but the full list is hardcoded
    23→- No way to toggle between full and restricted lists without code changes
    24→- The `createAndWrite*()` → `load*()` round-trip is redundant (hardcode → write → read)
    25→
    26→### Proposed Behavior
    27→
    28→1. Host spacecraft JSON files in the GitHub repo under `remote/spacecraft/`
    29→2. On boot, if WiFi is connected, fetch the latest JSON files from GitHub
    30→3. Cache fetched files on LittleFS; use cache if fetch fails
    31→4. If no cache and no network, fall back to a minimal hardcoded set
    32→5. A portal setting toggles between "Full" and "Restricted" spacecraft lists
    33→6. In restricted mode, only NASA-approved callsigns are displayed
    34→
    35→## Architecture
    36→
    37→### Remote File Hosting
    38→
    39→Host JSON files in the repository at `remote/spacecraft/`:
    40→
    41→```
    42→remote/
    43→└── spacecraft/
    44→    ├── names.json              # All callsign→name mappings
    45→    ├── blacklist.json          # Always-filtered callsigns
    46→    ├── restricted.json         # Array of NASA-approved callsigns (allowlist)
    47→    └── placeholder_rates.json  # Fallback uplink rates (until #37 removes need)
    48→```
    49→
    50→**Fetch URL pattern** (GitHub raw content):
    51→```

    54→
    55→Using `main` branch ensures the device always gets the latest published data. Could also use a tag or dedicated `data` branch for more control.
    56→
    57→### Data Flow
    58→

    61→ │
    62→ ├─ WiFi connected?
    63→ │   ├─ YES → Fetch remote JSONs from GitHub
    64→ │   │         ├─ Success → Write to LittleFS cache, load into memory
    65→ │   │         └─ Failure → Load from LittleFS cache (if exists)
    66→ │   │                       └─ No cache → Load hardcoded minimal fallback

   226→### Phase 2: Fetch + Cache System
   227→
   228→Add to `SpacecraftData`:
   229→
   230→```cpp
   231→// New public methods
   232→static bool fetchRemoteData();           // Fetch all files from GitHub
   233→static bool fetchAndCacheFile(           // Fetch single file
   234→    const char* filename,
   235→    const char* url
   236→);
   237→static bool hasCachedData();             // Check if LittleFS cache exists
   238→static void loadHardcodedFallback();     // Minimal hardcoded data
   239→
   240→// New private members
   241→static const char* baseUrl;  // "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GDKeller/JPL-MiniPulse/main/remote/spacecraft/"
   242→```
   243→
   244→**`fetchAndCacheFile()` implementation outline:**
   245→
   246→```cpp
   247→bool SpacecraftData::fetchAndCacheFile(const char* filename, const char* url) {
   248→    WiFiClientSecure secureClient;
   249→    secureClient.setInsecure();
   250→
   251→    HTTPClient http;
   252→    http.setFollowRedirects(HTTPC_FORCE_FOLLOW_REDIRECTS);
   253→    http.setTimeout(10000);
   254→
   255→    if (!http.begin(secureClient, url)) return false;
   256→
   257→    int httpCode = http.GET();
   258→    if (httpCode != HTTP_CODE_OK) {
   259→        http.end();
   260→        return false;
   261→    }
   262→
   263→    String payload = http.getString();
   264→    http.end();
   265→
   266→    // Validate it's parseable JSON before caching
   267→    DynamicJsonDocument testDoc(payload.length() * 1.5);
   268→    if (deserializeJson(testDoc, payload) != DeserializationError::Ok) {
   269→        Serial.printf("Invalid JSON from remote: %s\n", filename);
   270→        return false;
   271→    }
   272→
   273→    // Write to LittleFS cache
   274→    char filepath[64];
   275→    snprintf(filepath, sizeof(filepath), "/spacecraft_data/%s", filename);
   276→    File f = LittleFS.open(filepath, "w");
   277→    if (!f) return false;
   278→    f.print(payload);
   279→    f.close();
   280→
   281→    return true;
   282→}
   283→```
   284→
   285→**`fetchRemoteData()` implementation outline:**
   286→
   287→```cpp
   288→bool SpacecraftData::fetchRemoteData() {
   289→    const char* files[] = {"names.json", "blacklist.json", "restricted.json", "placeholder_rates.json"};
   290→    bool allSuccess = true;
   291→
   292→    for (const char* file : files) {
   293→        char url[256];
   294→        snprintf(url, sizeof(url), "%s%s", baseUrl, file);
   295→
   296→        Serial.printf("Fetching %s...\n", file);
   297→        if (!fetchAndCacheFile(file, url)) {
   298→            Serial.printf("Failed to fetch %s, will use cache\n", file);
   299→            allSuccess = false;
   300→        }
   301→    }
   302→
   303→    // Write fetch timestamp
   304→    File ts = LittleFS.open("/spacecraft_data/last_fetch.txt", "w");
   305→    if (ts) {
   306→        ts.print(millis());  // Uptime-based (no RTC)
   307→        ts.close();
   308→    }
   309→
   310→    return allSuccess;
   311→}
   312→```

---

## Implementation Plan: Optimize ESP32 Boot Sequence (ROADMAP #27)

### Investigation Findings

**Critical finding: The JSON files on flash are NEVER read back.** After exhaustive search, `names.json` and `blacklist.json` are only ever opened for writing (`"w"` mode). The `callsignToName()` and `checkBlacklist()` functions read exclusively from the in-memory `DynamicJsonDocument` objects (`spacecraftNamesJson` and `spacecraftBlacklistJson`), which are populated by direct assignment in the `createAndWrite*()` functions. The `serializeJson()` call writes the in-memory document to the file, but nothing ever reads those files back.

This means the flash writes are **pure waste** -- they serve no functional purpose. The files exist on disk but nothing ever reads them.

**Relationship to future work:** The remote spacecraft data plan (ROADMAP #41) will eventually change this architecture so that flash files *are* read (as a cache for remotely-fetched data). But that work is not yet done, and this optimization should be designed to be forward-compatible with that plan.

### Answers to the Design Questions

**Q1: Are the JSON files on flash ever read back?**
No. The in-memory `DynamicJsonDocument` objects are populated by direct key-value assignment in the `createAndWrite*()` functions. The `serializeJson()` call serializes that in-memory document to a LittleFS file, but no code ever opens those files for reading. The entire flash write path (including `FileUtils::createDir()`, `LittleFS.open("w")`, `serializeJson()`) is dead I/O.

**Q2: What's the simplest version check mechanism?**
Given that the files are never read, the simplest approach is to **stop writing them entirely** and just populate the in-memory documents. No version check needed. However, if we want to preserve the files on disk for future use (ROADMAP #41 compatibility), then a `/spacecraft_data/version.txt` file containing `currentFirmwareVersion` is the cleanest approach.

**Q3: Which delay() calls are safe to remove or reduce?**

| Line | Current | Purpose | Recommendation |
|------|---------|---------|----------------|
| 3352 | `delay(1000)` | LED test mode | Safe -- only runs when `testLEDs==true`, skip this optimization |
| 3488 | `delay(1000)` | Before portal start | Reduce to `delay(250)` -- WiFi connect is already handled by `wm.autoConnect()` with its own timeouts |
| 3503 | `delay(1000)` | After portal start | Reduce to `delay(250)` -- portal is non-blocking, just needs brief stabilization |
| 3515 | `delay(100)` | After `loadJson()` | Remove entirely -- no flash I/O to settle if we eliminate writes |
| 3522 | `delay(100)` | After color theme set | Remove entirely -- `setColorTheme()` sets in-memory values, no settling needed |
| 3564 | `delay(1000)` | Final boot delay | Reduce to `delay(100)` -- task creation and watchdog init don't need a full second |

### Recommended Approach: Two-Phase Strategy

Given the future plan for remote spacecraft data (ROADMAP #41), I recommend an approach that both optimizes boot now and prepares the architecture for that future work.

---

### Phase A: Eliminate Unnecessary Flash Writes (Primary Optimization)

**Strategy:** Separate "populate in-memory data" from "write files to flash." Since nothing reads the files, stop writing them on every boot. Keep the files on disk only when the firmware version changes (for diagnostic value and future ROADMAP #41 compatibility).

#### Step A1: Refactor `SpacecraftData` to separate concerns

In `lib/SpacecraftData/SpacecraftData.h`, add a new method and accept the firmware version:

```cpp
class SpacecraftData
{
    public:
    static void loadJson(const char* firmwareVersion);  // Changed signature
    static const char* callsignToName(const char* key);
    static bool checkBlacklist(const char* callsign);

    private:
    static void populateNamesInMemory();      // NEW: just populates DynamicJsonDocument
    static void populateBlacklistInMemory();   // NEW: just populates DynamicJsonDocument
    static void writeFilesToFlash();           // NEW: writes both files + version marker
    static bool shouldWriteFiles(const char* firmwareVersion);  // NEW: version check
    static DynamicJsonDocument spacecraftNamesJson;
    static DynamicJsonDocument spacecraftBlacklistJson;
};
```

#### Step A2: Implement `populateNamesInMemory()` and `populateBlacklistInMemory()`

In `lib/SpacecraftData/SpacecraftData.cpp`:

`populateNamesInMemory()` contains the exact same key-value assignments currently in `createAndWriteNamesFile()` (lines 22-103), but WITHOUT any file I/O:

```cpp
void SpacecraftData::populateNamesInMemory() {
    spacecraftNamesJson.clear();
    spacecraftNamesJson["ACE"] = "Advanced Composition Explorer";
    spacecraftNamesJson["PLC"] = "Akatsuki";
    // ... all existing assignments (lines 23-103 of current file) ...
    spacecraftNamesJson["Rate6"] = "Test Rate 6";
    Serial.println("Spacecraft names loaded into memory");
}
```

`populateBlacklistInMemory()` contains the assignments from lines 124-129:

```cpp
void SpacecraftData::populateBlacklistInMemory() {
    spacecraftBlacklistJson.clear();
    spacecraftBlacklistJson["TEST"] = true;
    spacecraftBlacklistJson["DSN"] = true;
    spacecraftBlacklistJson["RFC(VLBI)"] = true;
    spacecraftBlacklistJson["GO19"] = true;
    Serial.println("Spacecraft blacklist loaded into memory");
}
```

#### Step A3: Implement version-gated flash writes

```cpp
bool SpacecraftData::shouldWriteFiles(const char* firmwareVersion) {
    File versionFile = LittleFS.open("/spacecraft_data/version.txt", "r");
    if (!versionFile) {
        return true;  // No version file = first boot or fresh flash
    }
    
    char storedVersion[24] = {0};
    size_t bytesRead = versionFile.readBytes(storedVersion, sizeof(storedVersion) - 1);
    versionFile.close();
    
    if (bytesRead == 0) return true;
    
    return strcmp(storedVersion, firmwareVersion) != 0;
}

void SpacecraftData::writeFilesToFlash() {
    FileUtils::createDir("spacecraft_data");
    
    // Write names.json
    File namesFile = LittleFS.open("/spacecraft_data/names.json", "w");
    if (namesFile) {
        serializeJson(spacecraftNamesJson, namesFile);
        namesFile.close();
    }
    
    // Write blacklist.json
    File blacklistFile = LittleFS.open("/spacecraft_data/blacklist.json", "w");
    if (blacklistFile) {
        serializeJson(spacecraftBlacklistJson, blacklistFile);
        blacklistFile.close();
    }
    
    // Write version marker
    File versionFile = LittleFS.open("/spacecraft_data/version.txt", "w");
    if (versionFile) {
        versionFile.print(currentFirmwareVersion);  // Uses the extern
        versionFile.close();
    }
    
    Serial.println("Spacecraft data files written to flash");
}
```

#### Step A4: Update `loadJson()` to use the new flow

```cpp
void SpacecraftData::loadJson(const char* firmwareVersion) {
    Serial.println("Initializing spacecraft data...");
    
    // Always populate in-memory (fast, no I/O)
    populateNamesInMemory();
    populateBlacklistInMemory();
    
    // Only write to flash when firmware version changes
    if (shouldWriteFiles(firmwareVersion)) {
        Serial.println("Firmware version changed, writing spacecraft data to flash...");
        writeFilesToFlash();
        
        // Write version marker
        File versionFile = LittleFS.open("/spacecraft_data/version.txt", "w");
        if (versionFile) {
            versionFile.print(firmwareVersion);
            versionFile.close();
        }
    } else {
        Serial.println("Spacecraft data unchanged, skipping flash writes");
    }
}
```

#### Step A5: Update the call site in `src/main.cpp`

Line 3514 changes from:
```cpp
SpacecraftData::loadJson();
```
to:
```cpp
SpacecraftData::loadJson(currentFirmwareVersion);
```

#### Step A6: Remove `createAndWriteNamesFile()` and `createAndWriteBlacklistFile()`

These methods are no longer needed. Remove them from both the header and implementation. Also remove them from the public section of the class declaration.

---

### Phase B: Reduce `delay()` Calls

#### Step B1: Remove post-loadJson delay (line 3515)

```cpp
// BEFORE:
SpacecraftData::loadJson();
delay(100);

// AFTER:
SpacecraftData::loadJson(currentFirmwareVersion);
// delay removed - no flash I/O on normal boot, no settling needed
```

#### Step B2: Remove post-color-theme delay (line 3522)

```cpp
// BEFORE:
setColorTheme(FileUtils::config.miscellaneous.colorTheme);
delay(100);  // Small delay to allow bottom pixels to draw

// AFTER:
setColorTheme(FileUtils::config.miscellaneous.colorTheme);
// delay removed - setColorTheme only sets in-memory values
```

#### Step B3: Reduce WiFi-related delays (lines 3488 and 3503)

```cpp
// Line 3488 - BEFORE:
delay(1000); // Small delay to allow WiFi to connect

// AFTER:
delay(250);  // Brief stabilization before portal start

// Line 3503 - BEFORE:
delay(1000); // Small delay to allow WiFi to connect

// AFTER:
delay(250);  // Brief stabilization after portal start
```

#### Step B4: Reduce final boot delay (line 3564)

```cpp
// BEFORE:
delay(1000);

// AFTER:
delay(100);
```

---

### Phase C: Clean Up Dead Code (Optional, Relates to ROADMAP #23)

The commented-out `loadSpacecraftNamesProgmem()` and `loadSpacecraftBlacklistProgmem()` functions (lines 196-368 of `SpacecraftData.cpp`) are dead code from a previous PROGMEM approach. These could be removed as part of this work since we are already refactoring the file. However, this overlaps with ROADMAP #23 ("Remove commented-out code"), so it may be better to handle separately.

---

### Expected Boot Time Savings

| Source | Current Cost | After Optimization |
|--------|-------------|-------------------|
| `createAndWriteNamesFile()` flash I/O | ~200-400ms | 0ms (in-memory only) |
| `createAndWriteBlacklistFile()` flash I/O | ~50-100ms | 0ms (in-memory only) |
| `FileUtils::createDir()` x2 | ~50-100ms | 0ms (skipped) |
| `delay(100)` after loadJson (line 3515) | 100ms | 0ms (removed) |
| `delay(100)` after color theme (line 3522) | 100ms | 0ms (removed) |
| `delay(1000)` pre-portal (line 3488) | 1000ms | 250ms |
| `delay(1000)` post-portal (line 3503) | 1000ms | 250ms |
| `delay(1000)` final (line 3564) | 1000ms | 100ms |
| **Total estimated savings** | **~3.5-3.8s** | **~2.8-3.2s saved** |

On subsequent boots (same firmware version), the `shouldWriteFiles()` check adds only ~5-10ms for reading a tiny `version.txt` file.

---

### Edge Cases and Safety

1. **First boot / fresh flash:** `shouldWriteFiles()` returns `true` because `version.txt` does not exist. Files are written to flash and version marker is created. In-memory documents are populated regardless.

2. **OTA firmware update:** New firmware has a different `currentFirmwareVersion` string. `shouldWriteFiles()` returns `true` because stored version does not match. Files are rewritten with potentially new data.

3. **Corrupted version file:** If `version.txt` exists but is empty or unreadable, `shouldWriteFiles()` returns `true` (safe fallback -- writes files). No data loss possible.

4. **LittleFS format:** If the filesystem is formatted (`FORMAT_LITTLEFS_IF_FAILED`), all files are lost. `shouldWriteFiles()` returns `true` because `version.txt` is gone. Correct behavior.

5. **Forward compatibility with ROADMAP #41:** When remote spacecraft data is implemented, the `loadJson()` function will change to prefer cached remote data over hardcoded data. The `version.txt` file pattern can be repurposed or replaced by `last_fetch.txt`. The separation of "populate in-memory" from "write to flash" is architecturally compatible with the remote data plan's `loadHardcodedFallback()` concept.

---

### Implementation Sequence

1. **Modify `SpacecraftData.h`** -- Add new private methods, change `loadJson()` signature, remove old public methods
2. **Modify `SpacecraftData.cpp`** -- Implement `populateNamesInMemory()`, `populateBlacklistInMemory()`, `shouldWriteFiles()`, `writeFilesToFlash()`, updated `loadJson()`. Remove `createAndWriteNamesFile()` and `createAndWriteBlacklistFile()`.
3. **Modify `src/main.cpp`** -- Update `loadJson()` call site (line 3514), remove/reduce `delay()` calls (lines 3515, 3522, 3488, 3503, 3564)
4. **Build and verify** -- Run `~/.platformio/penv/bin/pio run` to ensure all environments compile
5. **Test on hardware** -- Verify first boot writes files, subsequent boots skip writes, OTA update triggers rewrite

---

   144→    if (showSerial) {

   152→            DevUtils::termColor("reset")
   153→        );

```text
     1→# Plan: Reduce Semaphore Hold Time (#25 / P5)
     2→
     3→## Context
     4→
     5→`parseData()` in `src/main.cpp` takes `freeListMutex` at line 2504 and holds it for the **entire XML parse loop** — potentially seconds — while the loop traverses stations/dishes/targets, calls `vTaskDelay(100ms)` four times, does blacklist/name lookups, Serial prints, and sends to the queue with a blocking `xQueueSend(100 ticks)`.
     6→
     7→Meanwhile, `freeSemaphoreItem()` on Core 1 only waits 500ms to acquire the mutex. If `parseData()` is mid-parse, the return fails silently and pool items are never reclaimed.
     8→
     9→**The mutex only needs to protect `freeList[]` and `freeListTop`** — the pool pop in `assignValuesToCraftSemaphore()` and pool push in `freeSemaphoreItem()`.
    10→
    11→## Approach: Three-Phase Lock Narrowing
    12→
    13→Restructure `parseData()` from one long critical section into three phases:
    14→
    15→### Phase 1 — Brief availability check (microseconds)
    16→```
    17→TAKE mutex
    18→  printSemaphoreList()          // reads freeList, must be inside lock
    19→  poolAvailable = (freeListTop >= 0)
    20→GIVE mutex                      // immediately
    21→if (!poolAvailable) return
    22→```
    23→Replaces lines 2503–2507. The `else` branch at line 2877 (pool empty) becomes the early return here.
    24→
    25→### Phase 2 — Parse with NO lock held (unchanged loop)
    26→The entire parse loop (lines 2513–2865) runs without holding the mutex. All `vTaskDelay()`, blacklist checks, name lookups, `findSignals()`, and Serial output execute freely.
    27→
    28→**Key change inside the target-found success path (lines 2766–2799):** Instead of calling `assignValuesToCraftSemaphore()` + `sendCrafToQueue()` inside the lock, validate `tempNewCraft` with `isValidCraftQueueItem(&tempNewCraft)`, set `breakParseLoop = true`, save counters, and break.

```md
# Plan: Optimize Boot Sequence (#27 / P7)

## Context

Boot time is ~15-20 seconds. The main culprits:
1. **SpacecraftData writes all JSON files to flash on every boot** — the data is hardcoded and can only change with a firmware update. The files are **never read back** from flash; `callsignToName()` and `checkBlacklist()` read exclusively from in-memory `DynamicJsonDocument` objects.
2. **~4.3s of `delay()` calls** in `setup()` — several are unnecessary or oversized.

## Approach

### A. Version-gated flash writes (primary optimization)

Separate "populate in-memory data" from "write to flash." Always populate in-memory (fast, no I/O). Only write to flash when firmware version changes, tracked via `/spacecraft_data/version.txt`.

This keeps files on disk for diagnostic value and forward-compatibility with ROADMAP #41 (remote spacecraft data caching).

### B. Reduce delay() calls

Remove or reduce unnecessary delays in `setup()`.

## Changes

### 1. `lib/SpacecraftData/SpacecraftData.h` — Update class interface

- Change `loadJson()` signature to accept `const char* firmwareVersion`
- Remove `createAndWriteNamesFile()` and `createAndWriteBlacklistFile()` from public API
- Add private methods: `populateNamesInMemory()`, `populateBlacklistInMemory()`, `shouldWriteFiles(const char*)`, `writeFilesToFlash(const char*)`

### 2. `lib/SpacecraftData/SpacecraftData.cpp` — Refactor implementation

**New `loadJson(const char* firmwareVersion)`:**
\```
1. populateNamesInMemory()       — same key=value assignments, no file I/O
2. populateBlacklistInMemory()   — same key=value assignments, no file I/O
3. if (shouldWriteFiles(firmwareVersion)):
     writeFilesToFlash(firmwareVersion)   — serialize both docs + write version marker
\```

**`populateNamesInMemory()`:** Extract lines 22–103 from current `createAndWriteNamesFile()` — the `spacecraftNamesJson[key] = value` assignments. No `LittleFS.open`, no `serializeJson`, no `FileUtils::createDir`.

**`populateBlacklistInMemory()`:** Extract lines 124–129 from current `createAndWriteBlacklistFile()` — the 4 blacklist assignments.

**`shouldWriteFiles(const char* firmwareVersion)`:**
- Open `/spacecraft_data/version.txt` for reading
- If file doesn't exist or is empty → return `true` (first boot / fresh flash)
- Read stored version, `strcmp()` against `firmwareVersion`
- Return `true` if different, `false` if match

**`writeFilesToFlash(const char* firmwareVersion)`:**
- `FileUtils::createDir("spacecraft_data")`
- Write `names.json` via `serializeJson(spacecraftNamesJson, file)`
- Write `blacklist.json` via `serializeJson(spacecraftBlacklistJson, file)`
- Write `version.txt` with `firmwareVersion`

**Delete:** `createAndWriteNamesFile()` and `createAndWriteBlacklistFile()` — fully replaced.

**Delete:** Commented-out PROGMEM functions (lines 196–368) — dead code, overlaps with ROADMAP #23.

### 3. `src/main.cpp` — Update call site + reduce delays

**Line 3514:** `SpacecraftData::loadJson()` → `SpacecraftData::loadJson(currentFirmwareVersion)`

**Delay reductions:**

| Line | Current | New | Rationale |
|------|---------|-----|-----------|
| 3488 | `delay(1000)` | `delay(250)` | WiFiManager has its own timeouts |
| 3503 | `delay(1000)` | `delay(250)` | Portal is non-blocking, brief stabilization sufficient |
| 3515 | `delay(100)` | Remove | No flash I/O on normal boot |
| 3522 | `delay(100)` | Remove | `setColorTheme()` sets in-memory values only |
| 3564 | `delay(1000)` | `delay(100)` | Task creation and watchdog init don't need a full second |

### 4. `board/ROADMAP-1.1.0.md` — Mark #27 DONE

## Edge Cases

- **First boot / fresh flash:** `version.txt` doesn't exist → `shouldWriteFiles()` returns true → files written
- **OTA firmware update:** Version string changes → files rewritten with new data
- **Corrupted version file:** Empty or unreadable → returns true (safe fallback, rewrites)
- **LittleFS format:** All files lost → `version.txt` gone → files rewritten

## Expected Savings

- Normal boot (same firmware): ~3-3.5s saved (no flash writes + reduced delays)
- First boot / firmware update: ~1.5-2s saved (delays reduced, writes still happen once)

## Verification

1. `~/.platformio/penv/bin/pio run -e release` — must compile clean
2. `~/.platformio/penv/bin/pio run -e debug` — must compile clean
3. Manual test: first boot should log "writing spacecraft data to flash"
4. Manual test: subsequent boot should log "skipping flash writes"
5. Manual test: after OTA update, should rewrite files
